    "output": "<path>/source/head/nodes/mikrotik_chr/chr-launch.sh</path>\n<type>file</type>\n<content>\n1: #!/bin/sh\n2: # chr-launch.sh: run the OFFICIAL mikrotik/chr image (MikroTik RouterOS Cloud\n3: # Hosted Router) as a containerlab node, image untouched.\n4: #\n5: # The image is MikroTik's own Docker Hub distribution (Alpine + qemu +\n6: # /diskimage/chr-<ver>.img + /start.sh). This script is bind-mounted into the\n7: # node and set as its entrypoint by the containerlab `mikrotik_chr` kind. It replaces\n8: # the image's /start.sh, which is not orchestration-ready (containerlab#3116):\n9: # it scans interfaces once before containerlab attaches the links, bridges the\n10: # management NIC so the container IP never reaches the router, and imports no\n11: # startup config.\n12: #\n13: # What it does (vrnetlab's mikrotik/routeros launch.py is the model, re-done\n14: # with the image's own busybox + qemu: no python, no ftp client, no tc):\n15: #   1. waits for the CLAB_INTFS data interfaces containerlab attaches (eth1..N)\n16: #   2. management, transparent: the container's eth0 is bridged with the VM's\n17: #      ether1 tap, and eth0's addresses and default gateways move into RouterOS\n18: #      ether1. The router IS the node's management address: every service and\n19: #      LLDP reach it directly, nothing is port-forwarded. The image ships only\n20: #      busybox (no tc), so this uses a bridge where vrnetlab uses tc-mirred\n21: #   3. data: one tap per container interface, bridged pairwise (ethN <-> tapN,\n22: #      LLDP forwarded). NIC order in the VM follows the eth index, so container\n23: #      ethN is always RouterOS ether(N+1), even with gaps\n24: #   4. after boot, over IPv6 link-local on the management bridge (no address is\n25: #      added to the management network): sets the credentials and the identity,\n26: #      configures ether1 with the management addresses and keeps their return\n27: #      path in its own routing table (`mgmt`, below), then fetches\n28: #      /ftpboot/config.auto.rsc (the containerlab startup-config, when present)\n29: #      from the launcher and `/import`s it\n30: #   5. prints the ready marker on the container log and waits on qemu\n31: #\n32: # Restart (docker restart, containerlab restart --node): RouterOS keys an\n33: # ethernet interface on its MAC. A NIC that comes back with a new MAC is a NEW\n34: # device (ether1 becomes ether3) and the DHCP client bound to ether1 never\n35: # binds. Docker re-rolls the container's eth0 MAC whenever the netns is\n36: # recreated, so the node id that seeds every NIC MAC and the data NIC count are\n37: # persisted in the container on the first boot and reused: the restarted qemu\n38: # carries the same NICs in the same order and RouterOS keeps ether1..N and\n39: # their config. The REST bootstrap is skipped on a restart; the management\n40: # step re-runs and re-applies the container's current addressing.\n41: #\n42: # Architectures: the image's own qemu (qemu-system-x86_64 on amd64,\n43: #   qemu-system-aarch64 + edk2 on arm64), KVM when /dev/kvm exists, else TCG.\n44: # Args (the kind's Cmd): --hostname H [--username U --password P]\n45: #   (unknown flags are ignored); credentials default to the USERNAME/PASSWORD env\n46: # Env (all optional, set under the node's `env:`); MEM, CPUS and DISK are the\n47: #   official image's own variables:\n48: #   MEM (qemu -m value, default 256 MiB + 8 MiB per data NIC and vCPU), CPUS (default 1),\n49: #   DISK (default 128M), CHR_INTF_WAIT (s, 60), CHR_BOOT_WAIT (s, 300)\n50: # Serial console: port 5000 inside the container\n51: #   (docker exec -it <node> nc 127.0.0.1 5000); the container itself has no\n52: #   address on the management network.\n53: # Ready: /.chr-launch-ready exists once RouterOS is ready (the kind's default\n54: #   healthcheck); it is removed at every start.\n55: # Log lines (docker logs clab-<lab>-<node>), all prefixed \"chr-launch:\":\n56: #   \"RouterOS ready\"                   login + startup config done\n57: #   \"startup config import FAILED: …\"  the router rejected the .rsc (RouterOS's\n58: #                                      own reason, with the line number)\n59: #   \"credential bootstrap FAILED: …\"   the user/password step failed\n60: #   \"management setup FAILED: …\"       the ether1 address / mgmt table step failed\n61: #\n62: # Copyright 2026 NetPilot Labs\n63: # Licensed under the BSD 3-Clause License.\n64: # SPDX-License-Identifier: BSD-3-Clause\n65: \n66: set -u\n67: \n68: # Credentials come from the USERNAME/PASSWORD env the kind sets (no quoting\n69: # limits on the password); --username/--password still override them.\n70: USERNAME=\"${USERNAME:-admin}\"\n71: PASSWORD=\"${PASSWORD-admin}\"\n72: HOSTNAME_ARG=\"\"\n73: while [ $# -gt 0 ]; do\n74:     case \"$1\" in\n75:         --username) USERNAME=\"$2\"; shift 2 ;;\n76:         --password) PASSWORD=\"$2\"; shift 2 ;;\n77:         --hostname) HOSTNAME_ARG=\"$2\"; shift 2 ;;\n78:         --connection-mode) shift 2 ;;\n79:         --trace) shift ;;\n80:         *) shift ;;\n81:     esac\n82: done\n83: [ -n \"$HOSTNAME_ARG\" ] || HOSTNAME_ARG=\"$(hostname)\"\n84: \n85: CPUS=\"${CPUS:-1}\"\n86: DISK=\"${DISK:-128M}\"\n87: INTF_WAIT=\"${CHR_INTF_WAIT:-60}\"\n88: BOOT_WAIT=\"${CHR_BOOT_WAIT:-300}\"\n89: INTFS=\"${CLAB_INTFS:-0}\"\n90: STARTUP_CFG=/ftpboot/config.auto.rsc\n91: # Per-container state in the rw layer: survives every restart, gone with the\n92: # container (destroy, redeploy --cleanup).\n93: DONE_MARKER=/.chr-launch-bootstrapped\n94: READY_FILE=/.chr-launch-ready\n95: ID_FILE=/.chr-launch-node-id\n96: NICS_FILE=/.chr-launch-nics\n97: MGMT_TABLE=mgmt\n98: # every management object the launcher creates carries this comment, so each\n99: # boot can find and re-apply them, and SaveConfig can leave them out\n100: MGMT_COMMENT=clab-mgmt\n101: MGMT_BR=br0\n102: # eth0's addressing as last seen: a launcher re-run in the same network\n103: # namespace finds eth0 already bridged and bare\n104: MGMT_FILE=/.chr-launch-mgmt\n105: SYSNET=/sys/class/net\n106: \n107: log() { echo \"chr-launch: $*\"; }\n108: rm -f \"$READY_FILE\"\n109: \n110: FETCH_PORT=8080\n111: \n112: # ---- disk -----------------------------------------------------------------\n113: IMG=\"\"\n114: for f in /diskimage/*.img; do [ -f \"$f\" ] && IMG=\"$f\" && break; done\n115: if [ -z \"$IMG\" ]; then\n116:     log \"no /diskimage/*.img in this image: not a RouterOS CHR image\"\n117:     exit 1\n118: fi\n119: # Only GROW the disk to the floor: an image already larger keeps its tail.\n120: disk_bytes() {\n121:     case \"$1\" in\n122:         *G|*g) echo $(( ${1%[Gg]} * 1024 * 1024 * 1024 )) ;;\n123:         *M|*m) echo $(( ${1%[Mm]} * 1024 * 1024 )) ;;\n124:         *K|*k) echo $(( ${1%[Kk]} * 1024 )) ;;\n125:         *) echo \"$1\" ;;\n126:     esac\n127: }\n128: want_bytes=\"$(disk_bytes \"$DISK\")\"\n129: cur_bytes=\"$(stat -c %s \"$IMG\" 2>/dev/null || wc -c < \"$IMG\")\"\n130: if [ \"$cur_bytes\" -lt \"$want_bytes\" ] 2>/dev/null; then\n131:     truncate -s \"$DISK\" \"$IMG\"\n132: fi\n133: \n134: # ---- wait for containerlab's data interfaces ------------------------------\n135: # shellcheck disable=SC2012  # interface names are ethN, ls is safe here\n136: count_intfs() { ls -d \"$SYSNET\"/eth[1-9]* 2>/dev/null | wc -l; }\n137: waited=0\n138: while [ \"$(count_intfs)\" -lt \"$INTFS\" ] && [ \"$waited\" -lt \"$INTF_WAIT\" ]; do\n139:     sleep 1\n140:     waited=$((waited + 1))\n141: done\n142: log \"interfaces: $(count_intfs) of $INTFS expected after ${waited}s\"\n143: \n144: # ---- qemu command line ----------------------------------------------------\n145: # The image's own qemu and firmware, as its /start.sh selects them.\n146: case \"$(uname -m)\" in\n147:     aarch64|arm64)\n148:         QEMU=\"qemu-system-aarch64 -M virt -pflash /usr/share/qemu/edk2-aarch64-code.fd\"\n149:         TCG_CPU=\"-cpu cortex-a57\" ;;\n150:     *)\n151:         QEMU=\"qemu-system-x86_64\"\n152:         TCG_CPU=\"\" ;;\n153: esac\n154: if [ -e /dev/kvm ]; then\n155:     ACCEL=\"-cpu host -accel kvm\"\n156: else\n157:     ACCEL=\"$TCG_CPU -accel tcg,split-wx=on\"\n158:     log \"no /dev/kvm: running under TCG emulation (slow boot)\"\n159: fi\n160: \n161: # MACs: unique per node AND per NIC. The container's eth0 MAC is unique per\n162: # node, so its LAST TWO octets identify the node; the NIC's last byte is the\n163: # interface index (00 = mgmt, 01 = ether2, …). Two nodes sharing a NIC MAC on\n164: # a link drop each other's frames as their own. The id is read on the FIRST\n165: # boot only and persisted (see Restart in the header).\n166: node_id=\"$(cat \"$ID_FILE\" 2>/dev/null)\"\n167: case \"$node_id\" in\n168:     [0-9a-f][0-9a-f]:[0-9a-f][0-9a-f]) ;;\n169:     *)\n170:         e=\"$(cat \"$SYSNET/eth0/address\" 2>/dev/null)\"\n171:         if [ -n \"$e\" ]; then\n172:             o2=\"${e##*:}\"; rest_mac=\"${e%:*}\"; o1=\"${rest_mac##*:}\"\n173:             node_id=\"$o1:$o2\"\n174:         else\n175:             node_id=\"$(hexdump -n2 -e '2/1 \"%02x:\"' /dev/urandom | sed 's/:$//')\"\n176:         fi\n177:         printf '%s\\n' \"$node_id\" > \"$ID_FILE\" 2>/dev/null \\\n178:             || log \"node id $node_id not persisted: a restart will renumber the NICs\"\n179:         ;;\n180: esac\n181: NET=\"-netdev tap,id=mgmt,ifname=tap0,script=no,downscript=no -device virtio-net,netdev=mgmt,mac=52:54:00:$node_id:00\"\n182: \n183: # ---- management: eth0 + tap0 on one bridge, eth0's addressing to the VM ----\n184: ip_global() { # ip_global <4|6> <dev>: the first global address/prefix\n185:     ip -\"$1\" addr show dev \"$2\" 2>/dev/null \\\n186:         | sed -n '/scope global/s/^ *inet6\\{0,1\\} \\([^ ]*\\) .*/\\1/p' | head -n1\n187: }\n188: ip_gw() { # ip_gw <4|6>: the default gateway\n189:     ip -\"$1\" route show default 2>/dev/null | sed -n 's/^default via \\([^ ]*\\) .*/\\1/p' | head -n1\n190: }\n191: M4=\"$(ip_global 4 eth0)\"; M6=\"$(ip_global 6 eth0)\"\n192: G4=\"$(ip_gw 4)\"; G6=\"$(ip_gw 6)\"\n193: if [ -n \"$M4$M6\" ]; then\n194:     printf 'M4=%s\\nM6=%s\\nG4=%s\\nG6=%s\\n' \"$M4\" \"$M6\" \"$G4\" \"$G6\" > \"$MGMT_FILE\" 2>/dev/null || true\n195: elif [ -f \"$MGMT_FILE\" ]; then\n196:     # shellcheck disable=SC1090  # written by this script, four plain assignments\n197:     . \"$MGMT_FILE\"\n198: fi\n199: log \"management: ${M4:-no IPv4}${M6:+, $M6} via ${G4:-no gateway}${G6:+, $G6}\"\n200: \n201: tunctl -t tap0 >/dev/null 2>&1 || ip tuntap add dev tap0 mode tap\n202: if [ ! -e \"$SYSNET/$MGMT_BR\" ]; then\n203:     _mtu=\"$(cat \"$SYSNET/eth0/mtu\" 2>/dev/null || echo 1500)\"\n204:     ip addr flush dev eth0\n205:     # The launcher's side of the bootstrap channel: IPv6 link-local on the\n206:     # bridge only. eth0 and tap0 are plain bridge ports.\n207:     sysctl -qw net.ipv6.conf.default.disable_ipv6=0 net.ipv6.conf.default.accept_ra=0 2>/dev/null\n208:     brctl addbr \"$MGMT_BR\"\n209:     brctl setfd \"$MGMT_BR\" 0 2>/dev/null\n210:     echo 16384 > \"$SYSNET/$MGMT_BR/bridge/group_fwd_mask\" 2>/dev/null\n211:     ip link set \"$MGMT_BR\" address \"52:54:01:$node_id:00\"\n212:     ip link set tap0 mtu \"$_mtu\"\n213:     ip link set \"$MGMT_BR\" mtu \"$_mtu\"\n214:     # eth0 joins the bridge only once ether1 is configured (mgmt_attach): until\n215:     # then nothing the router sends (its boot-time router advertisements, CHR's\n216:     # DHCP discovers) reaches the management network.\n217:     brctl addif \"$MGMT_BR\" tap0\n218:     sysctl -qw net.ipv6.conf.eth0.disable_ipv6=1 net.ipv6.conf.tap0.disable_ipv6=1 \\\n219:         \"net.ipv6.conf.$MGMT_BR.disable_ipv6=0\" \"net.ipv6.conf.$MGMT_BR.accept_ra=0\" \\\n220:         \"net.ipv6.conf.$MGMT_BR.router_solicitations=0\" 2>/dev/null\n221: fi\n222: ip link set tap0 up\n223: ip link set \"$MGMT_BR\" up\n224: # RouterOS's ether1 link-local address, from the MAC this script gives it\n225: VM_LL=\"fe80::5054:ff:fe${node_id%%:*}:${node_id##*:}00\"\n226: VM_EP=\"$VM_LL%$MGMT_BR\"\n227: # The bridge's own link-local address (the startup-config fetch source). Read\n228: # once qemu runs: until then tap0, the bridge's only port, has no carrier and\n229: # the address stays tentative.\n230: LL=\"\"\n231: bridge_ll() {\n232:     _w=0\n233:     while [ -z \"$LL\" ] && [ \"$_w\" -lt 20 ]; do\n234:         LL=\"$(ip -6 addr show dev \"$MGMT_BR\" 2>/dev/null | grep -v tentative \\\n235:             | sed -n 's/^ *inet6 \\(fe80::[^/]*\\)\\/64 .*/\\1/p' | head -n1)\"\n236:         [ -n \"$LL\" ] || { sleep 1; _w=$((_w + 1)); }\n237:     done\n238:     [ -n \"$LL\" ] || log \"no IPv6 link-local on $MGMT_BR\"\n239: }\n240: \n241: # NIC order = PCI order = the order of the -device args below. Walk\n242: # eth1..ethMAX so a gap (links on ether2 and ether5 only) keeps RouterOS\n243: # numbering aligned: a missing ethN still gets a tap, just no bridge. The count\n244: # never shrinks across restarts: a `docker restart` recreates the netns and\n245: # every lab veth of the node is gone, and a NIC absent for one boot loses the\n246: # config bound to it. The tap keeps ether(N+1) a real interface, its link comes\n247: # back when containerlab restores the veth or the lab is redeployed.\n248: max=0\n249: for d in \"$SYSNET\"/eth[1-9]*; do\n250:     [ -e \"$d\" ] || continue\n251:     n=\"${d##*/eth}\"\n252:     [ \"$n\" -gt \"$max\" ] && max=\"$n\"\n253: done\n254: prev=\"$(cat \"$NICS_FILE\" 2>/dev/null)\"\n255: case \"$prev\" in *[!0-9]*|\"\") prev=0 ;; esac\n256: [ \"$prev\" -gt \"$max\" ] && max=\"$prev\"\n257: # The wait above can end short of CLAB_INTFS on a large lab (links attach after\n258: # every container started): the NIC set still spans the expected count, and\n259: # the watcher bridges the late veths.\n260: case \"$INTFS\" in *[!0-9]*|\"\") INTFS=0 ;; esac\n261: [ \"$INTFS\" -gt \"$max\" ] && max=\"$INTFS\"\n262: [ \"$max\" -gt \"$prev\" ] && { printf '%s\\n' \"$max\" > \"$NICS_FILE\" 2>/dev/null || true; }\n263: \n264: # RouterOS v7 memory ≈ 256 + 8·CPUS·(ifaces) MiB (MikroTik CHR system\n265: # requirements). Scale by the HIGHEST generated NIC, not CLAB_INTFS: a sparse\n266: # link on ether64 means CLAB_INTFS=1 yet 63 data NICs are created below.\n267: if [ -z \"${MEM:-}\" ]; then\n268:     MEM=$((256 + 8 * CPUS * max))\n269: fi\n270: \n271: bridge_eth() { # bridge_eth <i>: container ethI joins brI beside tapI (brI made once)\n272:     _mtu=\"$(cat \"$SYSNET/eth$1/mtu\" 2>/dev/null || echo 1500)\"\n273:     if [ ! -e \"$SYSNET/br$1\" ]; then\n274:         brctl addbr \"br$1\"\n275:         ip link set \"br$1\" mtu \"$_mtu\"\n276:         ip link set \"tap$1\" mtu \"$_mtu\"\n277:         # forward LLDP (01:80:c2:00:00:0e, bit 14); STP/LACP cannot cross a bridge\n278:         echo 16384 > \"$SYSNET/br$1/bridge/group_fwd_mask\" 2>/dev/null\n279:         brctl addif \"br$1\" \"tap$1\"\n280:     fi\n281:     brctl addif \"br$1\" \"eth$1\"\n282:     ip link set \"eth$1\" up\n283:     ip link set \"br$1\" up\n284: }\n285: # A veth that lands or returns while qemu runs (containerlab restores a link\n286: # right after a restart --node, a large lab attaches late, a peer node's\n287: # redeploy recreates the pair) joins its bridge as it appears, so the RouterOS\n288: # interface behind tapN gets its link back without a restart here.\n289: watch_links() {\n290:     _warned=\"\"\n291:     while kill -0 \"$QEMU_PID\" 2>/dev/null; do\n292:         i=1\n293:         while [ \"$i\" -le \"$max\" ]; do\n294:             if [ -e \"$SYSNET/eth$i\" ] && [ ! -e \"$SYSNET/br$i/brif/eth$i\" ]; then\n295:                 bridge_eth \"$i\" && log \"link eth$i attached: bridged to tap$i\"\n296:             fi\n297:             i=$((i + 1))\n298:         done\n299:         for d in \"$SYSNET\"/eth[1-9]*; do\n300:             [ -e \"$d\" ] || continue\n301:             n=\"${d##*/eth}\"\n302:             [ \"$n\" -gt \"$max\" ] || continue\n303:             case \" $_warned \" in *\" $n \"*) continue ;; esac\n304:             _warned=\"$_warned $n\"\n305:             log \"link eth$n attached after qemu started with $max data NICs: no RouterOS interface for it until the node is restarted\"\n306:         done\n307:         sleep 2\n308:     done\n309: }\n310: \n311: i=1\n312: while [ \"$i\" -le \"$max\" ]; do\n313:     tap=\"tap$i\"\n314:     tunctl -t \"$tap\" >/dev/null 2>&1 || ip tuntap add dev \"$tap\" mode tap\n315:     [ -e \"$SYSNET/eth$i\" ] && bridge_eth \"$i\"\n316:     ip link set \"$tap\" up\n317:     mac=\"$(printf '52:54:00:%s:%02x' \"$node_id\" \"$((i & 255))\")\"\n318:     NET=\"$NET -netdev tap,id=d$i,ifname=$tap,script=no,downscript=no -device virtio-net,netdev=d$i,mac=$mac\"\n319:     i=$((i + 1))\n320: done\n321: \n322: # shellcheck disable=SC2086\n323: $QEMU $ACCEL -display none -monitor none \\\n324:     -m \"$MEM\" -smp \"cpus=$CPUS\" \\\n325:     -drive \"file=$IMG,format=raw\" \\\n326:     -serial telnet:0.0.0.0:5000,server,nowait \\\n327:     $NET &\n328: QEMU_PID=$!\n329: trap 'kill \"$QEMU_PID\" 2>/dev/null; wait \"$QEMU_PID\" 2>/dev/null; exit 0' TERM INT\n330: log \"qemu started (pid $QEMU_PID, mem ${MEM}M, cpus $CPUS, data nics $max)\"\n331: watch_links &\n332: \n333: # ---- REST helpers ---------------------------------------------------------\n334: json_str() { printf '%s' \"$1\" | sed 's/\\\\/\\\\\\\\/g; s/\"/\\\\\"/g'; }\n335: rest() { # rest <user:pass> <path> [json]\n336:     # Basic auth in a header, never in the URL: a password containing a URI\n337:     # delimiter (#, ?, /) would change where the authority ends. REST_T is the\n338:     # read timeout (default 20s).\n339:     _auth=\"Authorization: Basic $(printf '%s' \"$1\" | base64 | tr -d '\\n')\"\n340:     if [ $# -ge 3 ]; then\n341:         wget -q -O- -T \"${REST_T:-20}\" --header \"Content-Type: application/json\" \\\n342:             --header \"$_auth\" --post-data \"$3\" \"http://[$VM_EP]/rest/$2\" 2>/dev/null\n343:     else\n344:         wget -q -O- -T \"${REST_T:-20}\" --header \"$_auth\" \"http://[$VM_EP]/rest/$2\" 2>/dev/null\n345:     fi\n346: }\n347: # busybox wget discards the body of an HTTP error response, and RouterOS puts\n348: # its diagnosis ONLY there ({\"detail\":\"Script Error: … (line N column M)\"}; its\n349: # /log stays silent). So the calls whose failure must be readable go over a raw\n350: # HTTP POST through busybox nc. busybox nc exits the moment stdin hits EOF,\n351: # reply or not, and RouterOS keeps the connection open despite\n352: # `Connection: close`, so the request side is held open on a fifo and closed\n353: # once Content-Length bytes of body have arrived.\n354: resp_complete() { # resp_complete <file>: headers + Content-Length bytes of body arrived\n355:     _cl=\"$(grep -i -m1 '^Content-Length:' \"$1\" 2>/dev/null | tr -dc '0-9')\"\n356:     [ -n \"$_cl\" ] || return 1\n357:     grep -q -m1 '^\\r*$' \"$1\" 2>/dev/null || return 1\n358:     [ \"$(sed '1,/^\\r*$/d' \"$1\" | wc -c | tr -d ' ')\" -ge \"$_cl\" ]\n359: }\n360: rest_raw() { # rest_raw <user:pass> <path> <json> <timeout-s>  -> \"<status> <body>\"\n361:     _f=\"/tmp/chr-rest.$$\"; rm -f \"$_f\" \"$_f.out\"; mkfifo \"$_f\" || return 1\n362:     timeout \"$(( $4 + 5 ))\" nc \"$VM_EP\" 80 <\"$_f\" >\"$_f.out\" 2>/dev/null &\n363:     _pid=$!\n364:     exec 7>\"$_f\"\n365:     printf 'POST /rest/%s HTTP/1.1\\r\\nHost: [%s]\\r\\nAuthorization: Basic %s\\r\\nContent-Type: application/json\\r\\nContent-Length: %s\\r\\nConnection: close\\r\\n\\r\\n%s' \\\n366:         \"$2\" \"$VM_LL\" \"$(printf '%s' \"$1\" | base64 | tr -d '\\n')\" \\\n367:         \"$(printf '%s' \"$3\" | wc -c | tr -d ' ')\" \"$3\" >&7\n368:     _left=$4\n369:     while kill -0 \"$_pid\" 2>/dev/null && ! resp_complete \"$_f.out\" && [ \"$_left\" -gt 0 ]; do\n370:         sleep 1; _left=$(( _left - 1 ))\n371:     done\n372:     exec 7>&-\n373:     wait \"$_pid\" 2>/dev/null\n374:     _st=\"$(head -n1 \"$_f.out\" 2>/dev/null | tr -d '\\r' | cut -d' ' -f2)\"\n375:     _body=\"$(sed '1,/^\\r*$/d' \"$_f.out\" 2>/dev/null | tr -d '\\r')\"\n376:     rm -f \"$_f\" \"$_f.out\"\n377:     printf '%s %s' \"${_st:-000}\" \"$_body\"\n378: }\n379: # RouterOS REST returns the object/array on success and an empty body for a\n380: # bare `set`: only an explicit error object is a failure here. A silently\n381: # failed call is caught by the read-back checks that follow each step.\n382: is_err() { case \"$1\" in *'\"error\"'*) return 0 ;; *) return 1 ;; esac; }\n383: \n384: # ---- wait for RouterOS ----------------------------------------------------\n385: waited=0\n386: AUTH=\"\"\n387: # A fresh official CHR disk has ONLY the factory `admin` account (blank\n388: # password): the first boot authenticates as that account whatever --username\n389: # asks for, and the requested user is created below. On a restart the pair that\n390: # answers is the requested user.\n391: while [ -z \"$AUTH\" ]; do\n392:     for _cred in \"admin:\" \"admin:$PASSWORD\" \"$USERNAME:$PASSWORD\"; do\n393:         rest \"$_cred\" system/resource >/dev/null 2>&1 && { AUTH=\"$_cred\"; break; }\n394:     done\n395:     [ -n \"$AUTH\" ] && break\n396:     if ! kill -0 \"$QEMU_PID\" 2>/dev/null; then\n397:         log \"qemu exited during boot\"\n398:         exit 1\n399:     fi\n400:     sleep 2\n401:     waited=$((waited + 2))\n402:     if [ \"$waited\" -ge \"$BOOT_WAIT\" ]; then\n403:         log \"RouterOS did not answer within ${BOOT_WAIT}s: leaving qemu running\"\n404:         wait \"$QEMU_PID\"\n405:         exit 1\n406:     fi\n407: done\n408: log \"RouterOS answered after ${waited}s\"\n409: \n410: # Ready means a user can log in: RouterOS starts its SSH server well after REST\n411: # answers on a slow boot (about 40 s later under TCG on arm64), so when the\n412: # configuration keeps SSH enabled, its port must send the banner first.\n413: # A config that disables SSH is not waited for; a banner that never comes is\n414: # logged and the node is still declared ready (REST works).\n415: ssh_banner() { (sleep 3) | nc \"$VM_EP\" 22 2>/dev/null | head -c 7; }\n416: ready() {\n417:     case \"$(rest \"$AUTH\" \"ip/service?name=ssh\")\" in\n418:         *'\"disabled\":\"false\"'*)\n419:             _t0=$(date +%s)\n420:             until [ \"$(ssh_banner)\" = \"SSH-2.0\" ]; do\n421:                 if [ $(( $(date +%s) - _t0 )) -ge \"$BOOT_WAIT\" ]; then\n422:                     log \"SSH did not answer within $(( $(date +%s) - _t0 ))s (REST works)\"\n423:                     break\n424:                 fi\n425:                 sleep 2\n426:             done\n427:             ;;\n428:     esac\n429:     touch \"$READY_FILE\" 2>/dev/null || true\n430:     log \"RouterOS ready\"\n431: }\n432: \n433: # A failed step WITHHOLDS the ready marker (qemu keeps running, so the node can\n434: # still be inspected over the serial console, port 5000 in the container).\n435: bootstrap_fail() {\n436:     log \"credential bootstrap FAILED: $1\"\n437:     wait \"$QEMU_PID\"\n438:     exit 0\n439: }\n440: \n441: # ---- management: ether1 addressing and its own routing table ----------------\n442: # ether1 gets the container's management addresses, and their return path lives\n443: # in a `mgmt` routing table selected by a rule on those source addresses: a\n444: # default route the lab adds to `main` (a static 0.0.0.0/0, a PPPoE client's\n445: # default route, a dual-WAN pair) would otherwise take SSH/REST replies away\n446: # from the management network while the data plane works. CHR's default ether1\n447: # DHCP client is disabled: the address is static. *) return 1 ;; esac\n458: }\n459: rest_add() { # rest_add <what> <path> <json>: a 2xx with no error object, else mgmt_fail with the router's detail\n460:     _r=\"$(rest_raw \"$AUTH\" \"$2\" \"$3\" 20)\"\n461:     case \"$_r\" in\n462:         2??\\ *) is_err \"$_r\" && mgmt_fail \"$1: ${_r#* }\" ;;\n463:         *) mgmt_fail \"$1: ${_r:-no response}\" ;;\n464:     esac\n465: }\n466: rest_count() { # rest_count <path?query>: number of objects the GET answered\n467:     rest \"$AUTH\" \"$1\" | tr '{' '\\n' | grep -c '\"\\.id\"'\n468: }\n469: rest_clear() { # rest_clear <menu>: remove its clab-mgmt objects\n470:     _ids=\"$(rest \"$AUTH\" \"$1?comment=$MGMT_COMMENT\" | tr '{' '\\n' \\\n471:         | sed -n 's/.*\"\\.id\":\"\\([^\"]*\\)\".*/\\1/p' | paste -sd, -)\"\n472:     [ -z \"$_ids\" ] || rest_add \"remove old $1\" \"$1/remove\" \"{\\\".id\\\":\\\"$_ids\\\"}\"\n473: }\n474: # The tagged objects already match the container's addressing (a restart with\n475: # the same IP): leave them alone, re-applying would only drop live sessions.\n476: mgmt_in_place() {\n477:     _want=0\n478:     if [ -n \"$M4\" ]; then\n485:         rest_has \"ipv6/address?interface=ether1&address=$M6&comment=$MGMT_COMMENT\" || return 1\n486:         _want=$((_want + 1))\n487:     fi\n488:     [ \"$(rest_count \"ip/address?comment=$MGMT_COMMENT\")$(rest_count \"ipv6/address?comment=$MGMT_COMMENT\")\" \\\n489:         = \"$([ -n \"$M4\" ] && echo 1 || echo 0)$([ -n \"$M6\" ] && echo 1 || echo 0)\" ] || return 1\n490:     rest_has \"ipv6/nd?interface=ether1&ra-lifetime=none\" || return 1\n491:     [ \"$_want\" -gt 0 ]\n492: }\n493: mgmt_setup() {\n494:     if mgmt_in_place; then\n495:         log \"management on ether1 unchanged: ${M4:-no IPv4}${M6:+, $M6}\"\n496:         return 0\n497:     fi\n498:     for _m in routing/rule ip/route ipv6/route ip/address ipv6/address; do rest_clear \"$_m\"; done\n499:     rest_has \"routing/table?name=$MGMT_TABLE\" \\\n500:         || rest_add \"routing table $MGMT_TABLE\" routing/table/add \\\n501:             \"{\\\"name\\\":\\\"$MGMT_TABLE\\\",\\\"fib\\\":\\\"yes\\\",\\\"comment\\\":\\\"$MGMT_COMMENT\\\"}\"\n502:     _c=\"\\\"comment\\\":\\\"$MGMT_COMMENT\\\"\"\n503:     if [ -n \"$M4\" ]; then\n504:         _net4=\"$(ipcalc -n \"$M4\" | sed -n 's/^NETWORK=//p')/${M4#*/}\"\n505:         rest_add \"ether1 address $M4\" ip/address/add \"{\\\"address\\\":\\\"$M4\\\",\\\"interface\\\":\\\"ether1\\\",$_c}\"\n506:         rest_add \"route $_net4 in table $MGMT_TABLE\" ip/route/add \\\n507:             \"{\\\"dst-address\\\":\\\"$_net4\\\",\\\"gateway\\\":\\\"ether1\\\",\\\"routing-table\\\":\\\"$MGMT_TABLE\\\",$_c}\"\n508:         [ -z \"$G4\" ] || rest_add \"default via $G4 in table $MGMT_TABLE\" ip/route/add \\\n509:             \"{\\\"dst-address\\\":\\\"0.0.0.0/0\\\",\\\"gateway\\\":\\\"$G4\\\",\\\"routing-table\\\":\\\"$MGMT_TABLE\\\",$_c}\"\n510:         rest_add \"routing rule for ${M4%/*}\" routing/rule/add \\\n511:             \"{\\\"src-address\\\":\\\"${M4%/*}/32\\\",\\\"action\\\":\\\"lookup-only-in-table\\\",\\\"table\\\":\\\"$MGMT_TABLE\\\",$_c}\"\n512:     fi\n513:     if [ -n \"$M6\" ]; then\n544:         rest_has \"ip/address?interface=ether1&address=$M4\" || mgmt_fail \"$M4 not on ether1\"\n545:         rest_has \"routing/rule?src-address=${M4%/*}/32&table=$MGMT_TABLE\" \\\n546:             || mgmt_fail \"routing rule for ${M4%/*} not applied\"\n547:     fi\n548:     log \"management on ether1: ${M4:-no IPv4}${M6:+, $M6}, return path in routing table $MGMT_TABLE\"\n549: }\n550: # Join the management network, then have the router reach its gateway from the\n551: # management address: proves the return path both ways, and the ARP/ND request\n552: # refreshes the gateway's neighbor entry when the IP was used by another MAC\n553: # before (a redeployed lab hands out the same addresses).\n554: mgmt_attach() {\n555:     [ -e \"$SYSNET/$MGMT_BR/brif/eth0\" ] || brctl addif \"$MGMT_BR\" eth0\n556:     ip link set eth0 up\n557:     for _pair in \"$G4 ${M4%/*}\" \"$G6 ${M6%/*}\"; *) false ;; esac; do\n564:             if [ $(( $(date +%s) - _t0 )) -ge 30 ]; then\n565:                 log \"gateway $1 does not answer from $2 after $(( $(date +%s) - _t0 ))s (continuing)\"\n566:                 break\n567:             fi\n568:             sleep 1\n569:         done\n570:     done\n571: }\n572: \n573: # Bootstrap + startup-config import happen ONCE per container lifetime. then\n594:     if [ -n \"$PASSWORD\" ]; then\n595:         out=\"$(rest \"$FACTORY\" user/set \\\n596:             \"{\\\"numbers\\\":\\\"admin\\\",\\\"password\\\":\\\"$(json_str \"$PASSWORD\")\\\"}\")\"\n597:         is_err \"$out\" && bootstrap_fail \"set admin password: ${out:-no response}\"\n598:     fi\n599:     AUTH=\"admin:$PASSWORD\"\n600: else\n601:     out=\"$(rest \"$FACTORY\" user/add \\\n602:         \"{\\\"name\\\":\\\"$(json_str \"$USERNAME\")\\\",\\\"password\\\":\\\"$(json_str \"$PASSWORD\")\\\",\\\"group\\\":\\\"full\\\"}\")\"\n603:     is_err \"$out\" && bootstrap_fail \"create user $USERNAME: ${out:-no response}\"\n604:     AUTH=\"$USERNAME:$PASSWORD\"\n605:     # The factory `admin` still has a BLANK password and is reachable over the\n606:     # forwarded services: disable it so the node keeps no unauthenticated\n607:     # full-access account.\n608:     out=\"$(rest \"$AUTH\" user/set \"{\\\"numbers\\\":\\\"admin\\\",\\\"disabled\\\":\\\"yes\\\"}\")\"\n609:     is_err \"$out\" && bootstrap_fail \"disable factory admin: ${out:-no response}\"\n610:     if rest \"admin:\" system/resource >/dev/null 2>&1; then\n611:         bootstrap_fail \"factory admin still authenticates after disable\"\n612:     fi\n613: fi\n614: rest \"$AUTH\" system/resource >/dev/null 2>&1 \\\n615:     || bootstrap_fail \"the requested credentials do not authenticate\"\n616: out=\"$(rest \"$AUTH\" system/identity/set \"{\\\"name\\\":\\\"$(json_str \"$HOSTNAME_ARG\")\\\"}\")\"\n617: is_err \"$out\" && bootstrap_fail \"set identity: ${out:-no response}\"\n618: got=\"$(rest \"$AUTH\" system/identity)\"\n619: case \"$got\" in\n620:     *\"\\\"name\\\":\\\"$HOSTNAME_ARG\\\"\"*) : ;;\n621:     *) bootstrap_fail \"identity not applied: ${got:-no response}\" ;;\n622: esac\n623: \n624: mgmt_setup\n625: mgmt_attach\n626: \n627: # ---- startup config -------------------------------------------------------\n628: if [ -s \"$STARTUP_CFG\" ];         "text": "#!/bin/sh\n# chr-launch.sh: run the OFFICIAL mikrotik/chr image (MikroTik RouterOS Cloud\n# Hosted Router) as a containerlab node, image untouched.\n#\n# The image is MikroTik's own Docker Hub distribution (Alpine + qemu +\n# /diskimage/chr-<ver>.img + /start.sh). This script is bind-mounted into the\n# node and set as its entrypoint by the containerlab `mikrotik_chr` kind. It replaces\n# the image's /start.sh, which is not orchestration-ready (containerlab#3116):\n# it scans interfaces once before containerlab attaches the links, bridges the\n# management NIC so the container IP never reaches the router, and imports no\n# startup config.\n#\n# What it does (vrnetlab's mikrotik/routeros launch.py is the model, re-done\n# with the image's own busybox + qemu: no python, no ftp client, no tc):\n#   1. waits for the CLAB_INTFS data interfaces containerlab attaches (eth1..N)\n#   2. management, transparent: the container's eth0 is bridged with the VM's\n#      ether1 tap, and eth0's addresses and default gateways move into RouterOS\n#      ether1. The router IS the node's management address: every service and\n#      LLDP reach it directly, nothing is port-forwarded. The image ships only\n#      busybox (no tc), so this uses a bridge where vrnetlab uses tc-mirred\n#   3. data: one tap per container interface, bridged pairwise (ethN <-> tapN,\n#      LLDP forwarded). NIC order in the VM follows the eth index, so container\n#      ethN is always RouterOS ether(N+1), even with gaps\n#   4. after boot, over IPv6 link-local on the management bridge (no address is\n#      added to the management network): sets the credentials and the identity,\n#      configures ether1 with the management addresses and keeps their return\n#      path in its own routing table (`mgmt`, below), then fetches\n#      /ftpboot/config.auto.rsc (the containerlab startup-config, when present)\n#      from the launcher and `/import`s it\n#   5. prints the ready marker on the container log and waits on qemu\n#\n# Restart (docker restart, containerlab restart --node): RouterOS keys an\n# ethernet interface on its MAC. A NIC that comes back with a new MAC is a NEW\n# device (ether1 becomes ether3) and the DHCP client bound to ether1 never\n# binds. Docker re-rolls the container's eth0 MAC whenever the netns is\n# recreated, so the node id that seeds every NIC MAC and the data NIC count are\n# persisted in the container on the first boot and reused: the restarted qemu\n# carries the same NICs in the same order and RouterOS keeps ether1..N and\n# their config. The REST bootstrap is skipped on a restart; the management\n# step re-runs and re-applies the container's current addressing.\n#\n# Architectures: the image's own qemu (qemu-system-x86_64 on amd64,\n#   qemu-system-aarch64 + edk2 on arm64), KVM when /dev/kvm exists, else TCG.\n# Args (the kind's Cmd): --hostname H [--username U --password P]\n#   (unknown flags are ignored); credentials default to the USERNAME/PASSWORD env\n# Env (all optional, set under the node's `env:`); MEM, CPUS and DISK are the\n#   official image's own variables:\n#   MEM (qemu -m value, default 256 MiB + 8 MiB per data NIC and vCPU), CPUS (default 1),\n#   DISK (default 128M), CHR_INTF_WAIT (s, 60), CHR_BOOT_WAIT (s, 300)\n# Serial console: port 5000 inside the container\n#   (docker exec -it <node> nc 127.0.0.1 5000); the container itself has no\n#   address on the management network.\n# Ready: /.chr-launch-ready exists once RouterOS is ready (the kind's default\n#   healthcheck); it is removed at every start.\n# Log lines (docker logs clab-<lab>-<node>), all prefixed \"chr-launch:\":\n#   \"RouterOS ready\"                   login + startup config done\n#   \"startup config import FAILED: …\"  the router rejected the .rsc (RouterOS's\n#                                      own reason, with the line number)\n#   \"credential bootstrap FAILED: …\"   the user/password step failed\n#   \"management setup FAILED: …\"       the ether1 address / mgmt table step failed\n#\n# Copyright 2026 NetPilot Labs\n# Licensed under the BSD 3-Clause License.\n# SPDX-License-Identifier: BSD-3-Clause\n\nset -u\n\n# Credentials come from the USERNAME/PASSWORD env the kind sets (no quoting\n# limits on the password); --username/--password still override them.\nUSERNAME=\"${USERNAME:-admin}\"\nPASSWORD=\"${PASSWORD-admin}\"\nHOSTNAME_ARG=\"\"\nwhile [ $# -gt 0 ]; do\n    case \"$1\" in\n        --username) USERNAME=\"$2\"; shift 2 ;;\n        --password) PASSWORD=\"$2\"; shift 2 ;;\n        --hostname) HOSTNAME_ARG=\"$2\"; shift 2 ;;\n        --connection-mode) shift 2 ;;\n        --trace) shift ;;\n        *) shift ;;\n    esac\ndone\n[ -n \"$HOSTNAME_ARG\" ] || HOSTNAME_ARG=\"$(hostname)\"\n\nCPUS=\"${CPUS:-1}\"\nDISK=\"${DISK:-128M}\"\nINTF_WAIT=\"${CHR_INTF_WAIT:-60}\"\nBOOT_WAIT=\"${CHR_BOOT_WAIT:-300}\"\nINTFS=\"${CLAB_INTFS:-0}\"\nSTARTUP_CFG=/ftpboot/config.auto.rsc\n# Per-container state in the rw layer: survives every restart, gone with the\n# container (destroy, redeploy --cleanup).\nDONE_MARKER=/.chr-launch-bootstrapped\nREADY_FILE=/.chr-launch-ready\nID_FILE=/.chr-launch-node-id\nNICS_FILE=/.chr-launch-nics\nMGMT_TABLE=mgmt\n# every management object the launcher creates carries this comment, so each\n# boot can find and re-apply them, and SaveConfig can leave them out\nMGMT_COMMENT=clab-mgmt\nMGMT_BR=br0\n# eth0's addressing as last seen: a launcher re-run in the same network\n# namespace finds eth0 already bridged and bare\nMGMT_FILE=/.chr-launch-mgmt\nSYSNET=/sys/class/net\n\nlog() { echo \"chr-launch: $*\"; }\nrm -f \"$READY_FILE\"\n\nFETCH_PORT=8080\n\n# ---- disk -----------------------------------------------------------------\nIMG=\"\"\nfor f in /diskimage/*.img; do [ -f \"$f\" ] && IMG=\"$f\" && break; done\nif [ -z \"$IMG\" ]; then\n    log \"no /diskimage/*.img in this image: not a RouterOS CHR image\"\n    exit 1\nfi\n# Only GROW the disk to the floor: an image already larger keeps its tail.\ndisk_bytes() {\n    case \"$1\" in\n        *G|*g) echo $(( ${1%[Gg]} * 1024 * 1024 * 1024 )) ;;\n        *M|*m) echo $(( ${1%[Mm]} * 1024 * 1024 )) ;;\n        *K|*k) echo $(( ${1%[Kk]} * 1024 )) ;;\n        *) echo \"$1\" ;;\n    esac\n}\nwant_bytes=\"$(disk_bytes \"$DISK\")\"\ncur_bytes=\"$(stat -c %s \"$IMG\" 2>/dev/null || wc -c < \"$IMG\")\"\nif [ \"$cur_bytes\" -lt \"$want_bytes\" ] 2>/dev/null; then\n    truncate -s \"$DISK\" \"$IMG\"\nfi\n\n# ---- wait for containerlab's data interfaces ------------------------------\n# shellcheck disable=SC2012  # interface names are ethN, ls is safe here\ncount_intfs() { ls -d \"$SYSNET\"/eth[1-9]* 2>/dev/null | wc -l; }\nwaited=0\nwhile [ \"$(count_intfs)\" -lt \"$INTFS\" ] && [ \"$waited\" -lt \"$INTF_WAIT\" ]; do\n    sleep 1\n    waited=$((waited + 1))\ndone\nlog \"interfaces: $(count_intfs) of $INTFS expected after ${waited}s\"\n\n# ---- qemu command line ----------------------------------------------------\n# The image's own qemu and firmware, as its /start.sh selects them.\ncase \"$(uname -m)\" in\n    aarch64|arm64)\n        QEMU=\"qemu-system-aarch64 -M virt -pflash /usr/share/qemu/edk2-aarch64-code.fd\"\n        TCG_CPU=\"-cpu cortex-a57\" ;;\n    *)\n        QEMU=\"qemu-system-x86_64\"\n        TCG_CPU=\"\" ;;\nesac\nif [ -e /dev/kvm ]; then\n    ACCEL=\"-cpu host -accel kvm\"\nelse\n    ACCEL=\"$TCG_CPU -accel tcg,split-wx=on\"\n    log \"no /dev/kvm: running under TCG emulation (slow boot)\"\nfi\n\n# MACs: unique per node AND per NIC. The container's eth0 MAC is unique per\n# node, so its LAST TWO octets identify the node; the NIC's last byte is the\n# interface index (00 = mgmt, 01 = ether2, …). Two nodes sharing a NIC MAC on\n# a link drop each other's frames as their own. The id is read on the FIRST\n# boot only and persisted (see Restart in the header).\nnode_id=\"$(cat \"$ID_FILE\" 2>/dev/null)\"\ncase \"$node_id\" in\n    [0-9a-f][0-9a-f]:[0-9a-f][0-9a-f]) ;;\n    *)\n        e=\"$(cat \"$SYSNET/eth0/address\" 2>/dev/null)\"\n        if [ -n \"$e\" ]; then\n            o2=\"${e##*:}\"; rest_mac=\"${e%:*}\"; o1=\"${rest_mac##*:}\"\n            node_id=\"$o1:$o2\"\n        else\n            node_id=\"$(hexdump -n2 -e '2/1 \"%02x:\"' /dev/urandom | sed 's/:$//')\"\n        fi\n        printf '%s\\n' \"$node_id\" > \"$ID_FILE\" 2>/dev/null \\\n            || log \"node id $node_id not persisted: a restart will renumber the NICs\"\n        ;;\nesac\nNET=\"-netdev tap,id=mgmt,ifname=tap0,script=no,downscript=no -device virtio-net,netdev=mgmt,mac=52:54:00:$node_id:00\"\n\n# ---- management: eth0 + tap0 on one bridge, eth0's addressing to the VM ----\nip_global() { # ip_global <4|6> <dev>: the first global address/prefix\n    ip -\"$1\" addr show dev \"$2\" 2>/dev/null \\\n        | sed -n '/scope global/s/^ *inet6\\{0,1\\} \\([^ ]*\\) .*/\\1/p' | head -n1\n}\nip_gw() { # ip_gw <4|6>: the default gateway\n    ip -\"$1\" route show default 2>/dev/null | sed -n 's/^default via \\([^ ]*\\) .*/\\1/p' | head -n1\n}\nM4=\"$(ip_global 4 eth0)\"; M6=\"$(ip_global 6 eth0)\"\nG4=\"$(ip_gw 4)\"; G6=\"$(ip_gw 6)\"\nif [ -n \"$M4$M6\" ]; then\n    printf 'M4=%s\\nM6=%s\\nG4=%s\\nG6=%s\\n' \"$M4\" \"$M6\" \"$G4\" \"$G6\" > \"$MGMT_FILE\" 2>/dev/null || true\nelif [ -f \"$MGMT_FILE\" ]; then\n    # shellcheck disable=SC1090  # written by this script, four plain assignments\n    . \"$MGMT_FILE\"\nfi\nlog \"management: ${M4:-no IPv4}${M6:+, $M6} via ${G4:-no gateway}${G6:+, $G6}\"\n\ntunctl -t tap0 >/dev/null 2>&1 || ip tuntap add dev tap0 mode tap\nif [ ! -e \"$SYSNET/$MGMT_BR\" ]; then\n    _mtu=\"$(cat \"$SYSNET/eth0/mtu\" 2>/dev/null || echo 1500)\"\n    ip addr flush dev eth0\n    # The launcher's side of the bootstrap channel: IPv6 link-local on the\n    # bridge only. eth0 and tap0 are plain bridge ports.\n    sysctl -qw net.ipv6.conf.default.disable_ipv6=0 net.ipv6.conf.default.accept_ra=0 2>/dev/null\n    brctl addbr \"$MGMT_BR\"\n    brctl setfd \"$MGMT_BR\" 0 2>/dev/null\n    echo 16384 > \"$SYSNET/$MGMT_BR/bridge/group_fwd_mask\" 2>/dev/null\n    ip link set \"$MGMT_BR\" address \"52:54:01:$node_id:00\"\n    ip link set tap0 mtu \"$_mtu\"\n    ip link set \"$MGMT_BR\" mtu \"$_mtu\"\n    # eth0 joins the bridge only once ether1 is configured (mgmt_attach): until\n    # then nothing the router sends (its boot-time router advertisements, CHR's\n    # DHCP discovers) reaches the management network.\n    brctl addif \"$MGMT_BR\" tap0\n    sysctl -qw net.ipv6.conf.eth0.disable_ipv6=1 net.ipv6.conf.tap0.disable_ipv6=1 \\\n        \"net.ipv6.conf.$MGMT_BR.disable_ipv6=0\" \"net.ipv6.conf.$MGMT_BR.accept_ra=0\" \\\n        \"net.ipv6.conf.$MGMT_BR.router_solicitations=0\" 2>/dev/null\nfi\nip link set tap0 up\nip link set \"$MGMT_BR\" up\n# RouterOS's ether1 link-local address, from the MAC this script gives it\nVM_LL=\"fe80::5054:ff:fe${node_id%%:*}:${node_id##*:}00\"\nVM_EP=\"$VM_LL%$MGMT_BR\"\n# The bridge's own link-local address (the startup-config fetch source). Read\n# once qemu runs: until then tap0, the bridge's only port, has no carrier and\n# the address stays tentative.\nLL=\"\"\nbridge_ll() {\n    _w=0\n    while [ -z \"$LL\" ] && [ \"$_w\" -lt 20 ]; do\n        LL=\"$(ip -6 addr show dev \"$MGMT_BR\" 2>/dev/null | grep -v tentative \\\n            | sed -n 's/^ *inet6 \\(fe80::[^/]*\\)\\/64 .*/\\1/p' | head -n1)\"\n        [ -n \"$LL\" ] || { sleep 1; _w=$((_w + 1)); }\n    done\n    [ -n \"$LL\" ] || log \"no IPv6 link-local on $MGMT_BR\"\n}\n\n# NIC order = PCI order = the order of the -device args below. Walk\n# eth1..ethMAX so a gap (links on ether2 and ether5 only) keeps RouterOS\n# numbering aligned: a missing ethN still gets a tap, just no bridge. The count\n# never shrinks across restarts: a `docker restart` recreates the netns and\n# every lab veth of the node is gone, and a NIC absent for one boot loses the\n# config bound to it. The tap keeps ether(N+1) a real interface, its link comes\n# back when containerlab restores the veth or the lab is redeployed.\nmax=0\nfor d in \"$SYSNET\"/eth[1-9]*; do\n    [ -e \"$d\" ] || continue\n    n=\"${d##*/eth}\"\n    [ \"$n\" -gt \"$max\" ] && max=\"$n\"\ndone\nprev=\"$(cat \"$NICS_FILE\" 2>/dev/null)\"\ncase \"$prev\" in *[!0-9]*|\"\") prev=0 ;; esac\n[ \"$prev\" -gt \"$max\" ] && max=\"$prev\"\n# The wait above can end short of CLAB_INTFS on a large lab (links attach after\n# every container started): the NIC set still spans the expected count, and\n# the watcher bridges the late veths.\ncase \"$INTFS\" in *[!0-9]*|\"\") INTFS=0 ;; esac\n[ \"$INTFS\" -gt \"$max\" ] && max=\"$INTFS\"\n[ \"$max\" -gt \"$prev\" ] && { printf '%s\\n' \"$max\" > \"$NICS_FILE\" 2>/dev/null || true; }\n\n# RouterOS v7 memory ≈ 256 + 8·CPUS·(ifaces) MiB (MikroTik CHR system\n# requirements). Scale by the HIGHEST generated NIC, not CLAB_INTFS: a sparse\n# link on ether64 means CLAB_INTFS=1 yet 63 data NICs are created below.\nif [ -z \"${MEM:-}\" ]; then\n    MEM=$((256 + 8 * CPUS * max))\nfi\n\nbridge_eth() { # bridge_eth <i>: container ethI joins brI beside tapI (brI made once)\n    _mtu=\"$(cat \"$SYSNET/eth$1/mtu\" 2>/dev/null || echo 1500)\"\n    if [ ! -e \"$SYSNET/br$1\" ]; then\n        brctl addbr \"br$1\"\n        ip link set \"br$1\" mtu \"$_mtu\"\n        ip link set \"tap$1\" mtu \"$_mtu\"\n        # forward LLDP (01:80:c2:00:00:0e, bit 14); STP/LACP cannot cross a bridge\n        echo 16384 > \"$SYSNET/br$1/bridge/group_fwd_mask\" 2>/dev/null\n        brctl addif \"br$1\" \"tap$1\"\n    fi\n    brctl addif \"br$1\" \"eth$1\"\n    ip link set \"eth$1\" up\n    ip link set \"br$1\" up\n}\n# A veth that lands or returns while qemu runs (containerlab restores a link\n# right after a restart --node, a large lab attaches late, a peer node's\n# redeploy recreates the pair) joins its bridge as it appears, so the RouterOS\n# interface behind tapN gets its link back without a restart here.\nwatch_links() {\n    _warned=\"\"\n    while kill -0 \"$QEMU_PID\" 2>/dev/null; do\n        i=1\n        while [ \"$i\" -le \"$max\" ]; do\n            if [ -e \"$SYSNET/eth$i\" ] && [ ! -e \"$SYSNET/br$i/brif/eth$i\" ]; then\n                bridge_eth \"$i\" && log \"link eth$i attached: bridged to tap$i\"\n            fi\n            i=$((i + 1))\n        done\n        for d in \"$SYSNET\"/eth[1-9]*; do\n            [ -e \"$d\" ] || continue\n            n=\"${d##*/eth}\"\n            [ \"$n\" -gt \"$max\" ] || continue\n            case \" $_warned \" in *\" $n \"*) continue ;; esac\n            _warned=\"$_warned $n\"\n            log \"link eth$n attached after qemu started with $max data NICs: no RouterOS interface for it until the node is restarted\"\n        done\n        sleep 2\n    done\n}\n\ni=1\nwhile [ \"$i\" -le \"$max\" ]; do\n    tap=\"tap$i\"\n    tunctl -t \"$tap\" >/dev/null 2>&1 || ip tuntap add dev \"$tap\" mode tap\n    [ -e \"$SYSNET/eth$i\" ] && bridge_eth \"$i\"\n    ip link set \"$tap\" up\n    mac=\"$(printf '52:54:00:%s:%02x' \"$node_id\" \"$((i & 255))\")\"\n    NET=\"$NET -netdev tap,id=d$i,ifname=$tap,script=no,downscript=no -device virtio-net,netdev=d$i,mac=$mac\"\n    i=$((i + 1))\ndone\n\n# shellcheck disable=SC2086\n$QEMU $ACCEL -display none -monitor none \\\n    -m \"$MEM\" -smp \"cpus=$CPUS\" \\\n    -drive \"file=$IMG,format=raw\" \\\n    -serial telnet:0.0.0.0:5000,server,nowait \\\n    $NET &\nQEMU_PID=$!\ntrap 'kill \"$QEMU_PID\" 2>/dev/null; wait \"$QEMU_PID\" 2>/dev/null; exit 0' TERM INT\nlog \"qemu started (pid $QEMU_PID, mem ${MEM}M, cpus $CPUS, data nics $max)\"\nwatch_links &\n\n# ---- REST helpers ---------------------------------------------------------\njson_str() { printf '%s' \"$1\" | sed 's/\\\\/\\\\\\\\/g; s/\"/\\\\\"/g'; }\nrest() { # rest <user:pass> <path> [json]\n    # Basic auth in a header, never in the URL: a password containing a URI\n    # delimiter (#, ?, /) would change where the authority ends. REST_T is the\n    # read timeout (default 20s).\n    _auth=\"Authorization: Basic $(printf '%s' \"$1\" | base64 | tr -d '\\n')\"\n    if [ $# -ge 3 ]; then\n        wget -q -O- -T \"${REST_T:-20}\" --header \"Content-Type: application/json\" \\\n            --header \"$_auth\" --post-data \"$3\" \"http://[$VM_EP]/rest/$2\" 2>/dev/null\n    else\n        wget -q -O- -T \"${REST_T:-20}\" --header \"$_auth\" \"http://[$VM_EP]/rest/$2\" 2>/dev/null\n    fi\n}\n# busybox wget discards the body of an HTTP error response, and RouterOS puts\n# its diagnosis ONLY there ({\"detail\":\"Script Error: … (line N column M)\"}; its\n# /log stays silent). So the calls whose failure must be readable go over a raw\n# HTTP POST through busybox nc. busybox nc exits the moment stdin hits EOF,\n# reply or not, and RouterOS keeps the connection open despite\n# `Connection: close`, so the request side is held open on a fifo and closed\n# once Content-Length bytes of body have arrived.\nresp_complete() { # resp_complete <file>: headers + Content-Length bytes of body arrived\n    _cl=\"$(grep -i -m1 '^Content-Length:' \"$1\" 2>/dev/null | tr -dc '0-9')\"\n    [ -n \"$_cl\" ] || return 1\n    grep -q -m1 '^\\r*$' \"$1\" 2>/dev/null || return 1\n    [ \"$(sed '1,/^\\r*$/d' \"$1\" | wc -c | tr -d ' ')\" -ge \"$_cl\" ]\n}\nrest_raw() { # rest_raw <user:pass> <path> <json> <timeout-s>  -> \"<status> <body>\"\n    _f=\"/tmp/chr-rest.$$\"; rm -f \"$_f\" \"$_f.out\"; mkfifo \"$_f\" || return 1\n    timeout \"$(( $4 + 5 ))\" nc \"$VM_EP\" 80 <\"$_f\" >\"$_f.out\" 2>/dev/null &\n    _pid=$!\n    exec 7>\"$_f\"\n    printf 'POST /rest/%s HTTP/1.1\\r\\nHost: [%s]\\r\\nAuthorization: Basic %s\\r\\nContent-Type: application/json\\r\\nContent-Length: %s\\r\\nConnection: close\\r\\n\\r\\n%s' \\\n        \"$2\" \"$VM_LL\" \"$(printf '%s' \"$1\" | base64 | tr -d '\\n')\" \\\n        \"$(printf '%s' \"$3\" | wc -c | tr -d ' ')\" \"$3\" >&7\n    _left=$4\n    while kill -0 \"$_pid\" 2>/dev/null && ! resp_complete \"$_f.out\" && [ \"$_left\" -gt 0 ]; do\n        sleep 1; _left=$(( _left - 1 ))\n    done\n    exec 7>&-\n    wait \"$_pid\" 2>/dev/null\n    _st=\"$(head -n1 \"$_f.out\" 2>/dev/null | tr -d '\\r' | cut -d' ' -f2)\"\n    _body=\"$(sed '1,/^\\r*$/d' \"$_f.out\" 2>/dev/null | tr -d '\\r')\"\n    rm -f \"$_f\" \"$_f.out\"\n    printf '%s %s' \"${_st:-000}\" \"$_body\"\n}\n# RouterOS REST returns the object/array on success and an empty body for a\n# bare `set`: only an explicit error object is a failure here. A silently\n# failed call is caught by the read-back checks that follow each step.\nis_err() { case \"$1\" in *'\"error\"'*) return 0 ;; *) return 1 ;; esac; }\n\n# ---- wait for RouterOS ----------------------------------------------------\nwaited=0\nAUTH=\"\"\n# A fresh official CHR disk has ONLY the factory `admin` account (blank\n# password): the first boot authenticates as that account whatever --username\n# asks for, and the requested user is created below. On a restart the pair that\n# answers is the requested user.\nwhile [ -z \"$AUTH\" ]; do\n    for _cred in \"admin:\" \"admin:$PASSWORD\" \"$USERNAME:$PASSWORD\"; do\n        rest \"$_cred\" system/resource >/dev/null 2>&1 && { AUTH=\"$_cred\"; break; }\n    done\n    [ -n \"$AUTH\" ] && break\n    if ! kill -0 \"$QEMU_PID\" 2>/dev/null; then\n        log \"qemu exited during boot\"\n        exit 1\n    fi\n    sleep 2\n    waited=$((waited + 2))\n    if [ \"$waited\" -ge \"$BOOT_WAIT\" ]; then\n        log \"RouterOS did not answer within ${BOOT_WAIT}s: leaving qemu running\"\n        wait \"$QEMU_PID\"\n        exit 1\n    fi\ndone\nlog \"RouterOS answered after ${waited}s\"\n\n# Ready means a user can log in: RouterOS starts its SSH server well after REST\n# answers on a slow boot (about 40 s later under TCG on arm64), so when the\n# configuration keeps SSH enabled, its port must send the banner first.\n# A config that disables SSH is not waited for; a banner that never comes is\n# logged and the node is still declared ready (REST works).\nssh_banner() { (sleep 3) | nc \"$VM_EP\" 22 2>/dev/null | head -c 7; }\nready() {\n    case \"$(rest \"$AUTH\" \"ip/service?name=ssh\")\" in\n        *'\"disabled\":\"false\"'*)\n            _t0=$(date +%s)\n            until [ \"$(ssh_banner)\" = \"SSH-2.0\" ]; do\n                if [ $(( $(date +%s) - _t0 )) -ge \"$BOOT_WAIT\" ]; then\n                    log \"SSH did not answer within $(( $(date +%s) - _t0 ))s (REST works)\"\n                    break\n                fi\n                sleep 2\n            done\n            ;;\n    esac\n    touch \"$READY_FILE\" 2>/dev/null || true\n    log \"RouterOS ready\"\n}\n\n# A failed step WITHHOLDS the ready marker (qemu keeps running, so the node can\n# still be inspected over the serial console, port 5000 in the container).\nbootstrap_fail() {\n    log \"credential bootstrap FAILED: $1\"\n    wait \"$QEMU_PID\"\n    exit 0\n}\n\n# ---- management: ether1 addressing and its own routing table ----------------\n# ether1 gets the container's management addresses, and their return path lives\n# in a `mgmt` routing table selected by a rule on those source addresses: a\n# default route the lab adds to `main` (a static 0.0.0.0/0, a PPPoE client's\n# default route, a dual-WAN pair) would otherwise take SSH/REST replies away\n# from the management network while the data plane works. CHR's default ether1\n# DHCP client is disabled: the address is static. Everything is tagged\n# clab-mgmt and re-applied on every boot from the container's CURRENT addressing\n# (a restart can bring a new IP), while the bootstrap channel itself\n# (link-local) never depends on it.\nmgmt_fail() {\n    log \"management setup FAILED: $1 (redeploy the node: containerlab deploy --reconfigure)\"\n    wait \"$QEMU_PID\"\n    exit 0\n}\nrest_has() { # rest_has <path?query>: the GET answered a non-empty JSON array\n    case \"$(rest \"$AUTH\" \"$1\")\" in '['*'{'*) return 0 ;; *) return 1 ;; esac\n}\nrest_add() { # rest_add <what> <path> <json>: a 2xx with no error object, else mgmt_fail with the router's detail\n    _r=\"$(rest_raw \"$AUTH\" \"$2\" \"$3\" 20)\"\n    case \"$_r\" in\n        2??\\ *) is_err \"$_r\" && mgmt_fail \"$1: ${_r#* }\" ;;\n        *) mgmt_fail \"$1: ${_r:-no response}\" ;;\n    esac\n}\nrest_count() { # rest_count <path?query>: number of objects the GET answered\n    rest \"$AUTH\" \"$1\" | tr '{' '\\n' | grep -c '\"\\.id\"'\n}\nrest_clear() { # rest_clear <menu>: remove its clab-mgmt objects\n    _ids=\"$(rest \"$AUTH\" \"$1?comment=$MGMT_COMMENT\" | tr '{' '\\n' \\\n        | sed -n 's/.*\"\\.id\":\"\\([^\"]*\\)\".*/\\1/p' | paste -sd, -)\"\n    [ -z \"$_ids\" ] || rest_add \"remove old $1\" \"$1/remove\" \"{\\\".id\\\":\\\"$_ids\\\"}\"\n}\n# The tagged objects already match the container's addressing (a restart with\n# the same IP): leave them alone, re-applying would only drop live sessions.\nmgmt_in_place() {\n    _want=0\n    if [ -n \"$M4\" ]; then\n        rest_has \"ip/address?interface=ether1&address=$M4&comment=$MGMT_COMMENT\" || return 1\n        rest_has \"routing/rule?src-address=${M4%/*}/32&table=$MGMT_TABLE\" || return 1\n        [ -z \"$G4\" ] || rest_has \"ip/route?routing-table=$MGMT_TABLE&dst-address=0.0.0.0/0&gateway=$G4\" || return 1\n        _want=$((_want + 1))\n    fi\n    if [ -n \"$M6\" ]; then\n        rest_has \"ipv6/address?interface=ether1&address=$M6&comment=$MGMT_COMMENT\" || return 1\n        _want=$((_want + 1))\n    fi\n    [ \"$(rest_count \"ip/address?comment=$MGMT_COMMENT\")$(rest_count \"ipv6/address?comment=$MGMT_COMMENT\")\" \\\n        = \"$([ -n \"$M4\" ] && echo 1 || echo 0)$([ -n \"$M6\" ] && echo 1 || echo 0)\" ] || return 1\n    rest_has \"ipv6/nd?interface=ether1&ra-lifetime=none\" || return 1\n    [ \"$_want\" -gt 0 ]\n}\nmgmt_setup() {\n    if mgmt_in_place; then\n        log \"management on ether1 unchanged: ${M4:-no IPv4}${M6:+, $M6}\"\n        return 0\n    fi\n    for _m in routing/rule ip/route ipv6/route ip/address ipv6/address; do rest_clear \"$_m\"; done\n    rest_has \"routing/table?name=$MGMT_TABLE\" \\\n        || rest_add \"routing table $MGMT_TABLE\" routing/table/add \\\n            \"{\\\"name\\\":\\\"$MGMT_TABLE\\\",\\\"fib\\\":\\\"yes\\\",\\\"comment\\\":\\\"$MGMT_COMMENT\\\"}\"\n    _c=\"\\\"comment\\\":\\\"$MGMT_COMMENT\\\"\"\n    if [ -n \"$M4\" ]; then\n        _net4=\"$(ipcalc -n \"$M4\" | sed -n 's/^NETWORK=//p')/${M4#*/}\"\n        rest_add \"ether1 address $M4\" ip/address/add \"{\\\"address\\\":\\\"$M4\\\",\\\"interface\\\":\\\"ether1\\\",$_c}\"\n        rest_add \"route $_net4 in table $MGMT_TABLE\" ip/route/add \\\n            \"{\\\"dst-address\\\":\\\"$_net4\\\",\\\"gateway\\\":\\\"ether1\\\",\\\"routing-table\\\":\\\"$MGMT_TABLE\\\",$_c}\"\n        [ -z \"$G4\" ] || rest_add \"default via $G4 in table $MGMT_TABLE\" ip/route/add \\\n            \"{\\\"dst-address\\\":\\\"0.0.0.0/0\\\",\\\"gateway\\\":\\\"$G4\\\",\\\"routing-table\\\":\\\"$MGMT_TABLE\\\",$_c}\"\n        rest_add \"routing rule for ${M4%/*}\" routing/rule/add \\\n            \"{\\\"src-address\\\":\\\"${M4%/*}/32\\\",\\\"action\\\":\\\"lookup-only-in-table\\\",\\\"table\\\":\\\"$MGMT_TABLE\\\",$_c}\"\n    fi\n    if [ -n \"$M6\" ]; Reasoning
Default restart policy is empty for most node kinds (only linux/tailscale set "always"). For VRNode-based kinds, restart policy is empty → docker treats empty as "no" (default). So an unhealthy container isn't restarted automatically. Good — no automatic restart loop. But the unhealthy status remains visible, which is exactly what the launcher design says ("withholds the ready marker" — the node stays unhealthy, expected). So the StartPeriod=300 vs BOOT_WAIT=300 concern: with restart policy "no" (docker default when empty), the impact is just health status "unhealthy" after ~315s. That matches the documented failure mode ("withholds the ready marker"). Actually wait — the start period only delays retry counting; with Retries=3 and Interval=5, unhealthy happens ~315s after start. If boot takes longer than 300 (TCG), healthcheck turns unhealthy while launcher still booting — but that's also exactly what happens with any failure; and users can override the healthcheck. Minor, not a defect worth reporting? The window where a *slow but successful* boot shows unhealthy is real. The r1 robot test waits up to 420s for health. If TCG boot takes >315s on CI, the container would show unhealthy and the robot "Wait until healthy" keyword fails even though the node eventually becomes healthy (it stays unhealthy until next check? No — once READY_FILE is touched, next interval check passes → healthy again, interval 5s). So transient. Not worth a finding; maybe P4 note. I'll leave it out or as coverage note.

Now let me read the remaining files: the CI workflow new file, cicd.yml diff region, docs page, index.md, mkdocs.yml entries, test fixtures (topology, robot, rsc files), and schema diff regions. Also verify docs anchor `../vrnetlab.md#management-interface` and `../topo-def-file.md#interface-naming`.

1: ---
2: search:
3:   boost: 4
4: kind_code_name: mikrotik_chr
5: kind_display_name: MikroTik RouterOS CHR
6: ---
7: # -{{ kind_display_name }}-
8: 
9: [MikroTik RouterOS](https://mikrotik.com/software) Cloud Hosted Router (CHR) from the **official [`mikrotik/chr`](https://hub.docker.com/r/mikrotik/chr) image** is identified with the `-{{ kind_code_name }}-` kind in the [topology file](../topo-def-file.md). The image is published by MikroTik for `amd64` and `arm64` and is used as is: no [vrnetlab](../vrnetlab.md) build is needed.
10: 
11: The image is a QEMU VM (Alpine, qemu and the CHR disk) in a container. Its own `/start.sh` is not made for orchestrated links ([#3116](https://github.com/srl-labs/containerlab/issues/3116)), so the kind writes a launcher script into the node's lab directory, mounts it read-only and runs it as the entrypoint instead. The launcher uses only the tools that ship in the image.
12: 
13: /// note
14: The [`mikrotik_ros`](vr-ros.md) kind runs CHR from an image you build with vrnetlab. Both kinds use the same interface naming and startup config format, so a lab moves from one to the other by changing `kind` and `image`.
15: ///
16: 
17: ## Getting -{{ kind_display_name }}- image
18: 
19: ```bash
20: docker pull mikrotik/chr:7.24.5
21: ```
22: 
23: Tags follow RouterOS versions, plus `stable`, `long-term`, `testing` and `development`. This kind has been tested with 7.24.5 (stable), 7.23.8 (long-term) and 7.25rc2 (testing).
24: 
25: ## Managing -{{ kind_display_name }}- nodes
26: 
27: /// tab | CLI
28: ```bash
29: ssh admin@<node-name>
30: ```
31: ///
32: /// tab | REST API
33: ```bash
34: curl -u admin:admin http://<node-name>/rest/system/resource
35: ```
36: ///
37: /// tab | Winbox / API
38: Winbox (TCP 8291) and the RouterOS API (TCP 8728, 8729 for TLS) are reachable on the node's management address.
39: ///
40: /// tab | Console
41: The serial console is on port 5000 inside the container:
42: ```bash
43: docker exec -it <node-name> nc 127.0.0.1 5000
44: ```
45: ///
46: /// tab | bash
47: ```bash
48: docker exec -it <node-name> sh
49: ```
50: ///
51: 
52: The node's management address is RouterOS's own `ether1` address ([transparent management](#management-connectivity)), so every service RouterOS runs answers on it directly, with nothing forwarded.
53: 
54: /// note
55: Default credentials are `admin:admin`. With custom [`credentials`](../nodes.md#credentials) the kind creates that user in the `full` group and disables the factory `admin` account, which has a blank password on a fresh CHR disk.
56: ///
57: 
58: ## Interface naming
59: 
60: You can use [interface names](../topo-def-file.md#interface-naming) in the topology file like they appear in RouterOS: `etherX`, where `X` is the port number.
61: 
62: * `ether2` - first data port
63: * `ether3` - second data port, and so on
64: 
65: /// admonition
66:     type: warning
67: Data ports start at `ether2`: `ether1` is the management interface. Using `ether1` in a topology results in an error.
68: ///
69: 
70: The container interface `ethN` is RouterOS `ether(N+1)`, also when links leave gaps: a link on `eth12` alone still lands on `ether13`, with `ether2` to `ether12` present and unlinked. Interface MTU follows the link MTU, and LLDP frames are forwarded, so `/ip neighbor` shows the peers.
71: 
72: ## Node configuration
73: 
74: -{{ kind_display_name }}- nodes boot with the default CHR configuration plus the credentials, the identity (set to the node name) and the management setup described below.
75: 
76: ### Startup configuration
77: 
78: A RouterOS script (`.rsc`) set with [`startup-config`](../nodes.md#startup-config) is imported once the router is up:
79: 
80: ```yaml
81: name: chr_lab
82: topology:
83:   nodes:
84:     r1:
85:       kind: mikrotik_chr
86:       image: mikrotik/chr:7.24.5
87:       startup-config: r1.rsc
88: ```
89: 
90: The file is copied to the node's lab directory as `ftpboot/config.auto.rsc` and imported over the REST API. RouterOS imports line by line and stops at the first error: in that case the container log carries RouterOS's own reason with the line number, for example
91: 
92: ```
93: chr-launch: startup config import FAILED: Script Error: bad parameter network-type (line 3 column 59); lines before the failing one were applied, the rest were not
94: ```
95: 
96: and the node does not become ready.
97: 
98: ### Saving configuration
99: 
100: [`containerlab save`](../../cmd/save.md) writes each node's `/export` to `ftpboot/config.auto.rsc` in its lab directory. The management objects the launcher creates at every boot (everything tagged `clab-mgmt`, and the `ether1` DHCP client) are left out, so the saved file can be used as the startup config of the next deployment, also one with different management addresses.
101: 
102: ### Node readiness
103: 
104: The node is ready once RouterOS accepted the credentials and the startup config, reaches its gateway from the management address and, unless the configuration disables SSH, its SSH server answers. An SSH server that does not answer within `CHR_BOOT_WAIT` is logged, and the node is still declared ready, since REST and the console work. The container log then shows
105: 
106: ```
107: chr-launch: RouterOS ready
108: ```
109: 
110: and the kind's default [healthcheck](../nodes.md#healthcheck) reports the container `healthy`, so [`stages`](../nodes.md#stages) with `wait-for` can depend on it. A node whose startup config was rejected never becomes healthy. A `healthcheck` set in the topology replaces the default one.
111: 
112: ### Resources
113: 
114: The kind reads the official image's own environment variables:
115: 
116: | Variable | Default | Purpose |
117: |----------|---------|---------|
118: | `MEM` | 256 MiB + 8 MiB per data interface and vCPU | VM memory (a QEMU `-m` value, e.g. `1024` or `1G`) |
119: | `CPUS` | `1` | VM vCPUs |
120: | `DISK` | `128M` | minimum disk size (the disk only grows) |
121: | `CHR_INTF_WAIT` | `60` | seconds to wait for the data interfaces containerlab attaches before the VM starts |
122: | `CHR_BOOT_WAIT` | `300` | seconds to wait for RouterOS to answer, for the startup config import, and for SSH before the node is declared ready |
123: 
124: ```yaml
125: r1:
126:   kind: mikrotik_chr
127:   image: mikrotik/chr:7.24.5
128:   env:
129:     MEM: 1024
130:     CPUS: 2
131: ```
132: 
133: KVM is used when `/dev/kvm` is available. Without it the image's QEMU runs under TCG emulation: the node works, but boots several times slower.
134: 
135: ## Management connectivity
136: 
137: Management is transparent: the IPv4 and IPv6 addresses and gateways containerlab gives the node's `eth0` are configured on RouterOS `ether1`, and the container's `eth0` is bridged to the VM's `ether1`. The router is the node's management address: SSH, the REST API, Winbox, SNMP and every other service answer on it, LLDP/MNDP work on the management network, and the address in the topology table is the one in the RouterOS configuration.
138: 
139: The image ships busybox only (no `tc`), so where vrnetlab's [transparent management](../vrnetlab.md#management-interface) redirects with tc-mirred, this kind uses a Linux bridge. The container itself has no address on the management network; it reaches RouterOS for bootstrap over IPv6 link-local on that bridge.
140: 
141: The management return path lives in its own routing table, `mgmt`, selected by routing rules for the management addresses, and CHR's `ether1` DHCP client is disabled. A default route in the lab configuration, a PPPoE client's default route or a dual-WAN setup in `main` therefore does not cut SSH or REST access to the node. RouterOS's router advertisements on `ether1` carry a zero router lifetime, so no host on the management network takes the router as its IPv6 default gateway; the container joins the management network only once this is in place. The objects carry the comment `clab-mgmt` and are re-applied at boot when the container's addressing changed.
142: 
143: /// warning
144: Do not remove or change the `clab-mgmt` objects or the `mgmt` routing table: management of the node depends on them.
145: ///
146: 
147: ## Restarts
148: 
149: [`containerlab restart`](../../cmd/restart.md) and a `/system reboot` inside RouterOS keep the interface names, MAC addresses, configuration and links: the launcher persists the NIC identity in the container on first boot and does not re-run the bootstrap. A plain `docker restart` keeps the router and its management, but Docker deletes the node's veth links, which stay down until the node is restarted with containerlab or the lab is redeployed.
150: 
151: ## File mounts
152: 
153: For each node containerlab creates in its [lab directory](../conf-artifacts.md):
154: 
155: * `ftpboot/` - mounted to `/ftpboot`, holds `config.auto.rsc`
156: * `chr-launch.sh` - the launcher, mounted read-only to `/chr-launch.sh` and rewritten on every deploy

(End of file - total 156 lines)
</content>

This kind has been tested with 7.24.5 (stable), 7.23.8 (long-term) and 7.25rc2 (testing).\n24: \n25: ## Managing -{{ kind_display_name }}- nodes\n26: \n27: /// tab | CLI\n28: ```bash\n29: ssh admin@<node-name>\n30: ```\n31: ///\n32: /// tab | REST API\n33: ```bash\n34: curl -u admin:admin http://<node-name>/rest/system/resource\n35: ```\n36: ///\n37: /// tab | Winbox / API\n38: Winbox (TCP 8291) and the RouterOS API (TCP 8728, 8729 for TLS) are reachable on the node's management address.\n39: ///\n40: /// tab | Console\n41: The serial console is on port 5000 inside the container:\n42: ```bash\n43: docker exec -it <node-name> nc 127.0.0.1 5000\n44: ```\n45: ///\n46: /// tab | bash\n47: ```bash\n48: docker exec -it <node-name> sh\n49: ```\n50: ///\n51: \n52: The node's management address is RouterOS's own `ether1` address ([transparent management](#management-connectivity)), so every service RouterOS runs answers on it directly, with nothing forwarded.\n53: \n54: /// note\n55: Default credentials are `admin:admin`. With custom [`credentials`](../nodes.md#credentials) the kind creates that user in the `full` group and disables the factory `admin` account, which has a blank password on a fresh CHR disk.\n56: ///\n57: \n58: ## Interface naming\n59: \n60: You can use [interface names](../topo-def-file.md#interface-naming) in the topology file like they appear in RouterOS: `etherX`, where `X` is the port number.\n61: \n62: * `ether2` - first data port\n63: * `ether3` - second data port, and so on\n64: \n65: /// admonition\n66:     type: warning\n67: Data ports start at `ether2`: `ether1` is the management interface. Using `ether1` in a topology results in an error.\n68: ///\n69: \n70: The container interface `ethN` is RouterOS `ether(N+1)`, also when links leave gaps: a link on `eth12` alone still lands on `ether13`, with `ether2` to `ether12` present and unlinked. Interface MTU follows the link MTU, and LLDP frames are forwarded, so `/ip neighbor` shows the peers.\n71: \n72: ## Node configuration\n73: \n74: -{{ kind_display_name }}- nodes boot with the default CHR configuration plus the credentials, the identity (set to the node name) and the management setup described below.\n75: \n76: ### Startup configuration\n77: \n78: A RouterOS script (`.rsc`) set with [`startup-config`](../nodes.md#startup-config) is imported once the router is up:\n79: \n80: ```yaml\n81: name: chr_lab\n82: topology:\n83:   nodes:\n84:     r1:\n85:       kind: mikrotik_chr\n86:       image: mikrotik/chr:7.24.5\n87:       startup-config: r1.rsc\n88: ```\n89: \n90: The file is copied to the node's lab directory as `ftpboot/config.auto.rsc` and imported over the REST API. RouterOS imports line by line and stops at the first error: in that case the container log carries RouterOS's own reason with the line number, for example\n91: \n92: ```\n93: chr-launch: startup config import FAILED: Script Error: bad parameter network-type (line 3 column 59); lines before the failing one were applied, the rest were not\n94: ```\n95: \n96: and the node does not become ready.\n97: \n98: ### Saving configuration\n99: \n100: [`containerlab save`](../../cmd/save.md) writes each node's `/export` to `ftpboot/config.auto.rsc` in its lab directory. The management objects the launcher creates at every boot (everything tagged `clab-mgmt`, and the `ether1` DHCP client) are left out, so the saved file can be used as the startup config of the next deployment, also one with different management addresses.\n101: \n102: ### Node readiness\n103: \n104: The node is ready once RouterOS accepted the credentials and the startup config, reaches its gateway from the management address and, unless the configuration disables SSH, its SSH server answers. An SSH server that does not answer within `CHR_BOOT_WAIT` is logged, and the node is still declared ready, since REST and the console work. The container log then shows\n105: \n106: ```\n107: chr-launch: RouterOS ready\n108: ```\n109: \n110: and the kind's default [healthcheck](../nodes.md#healthcheck) reports the container `healthy`, so [`stages`](../nodes.md#stages) with `wait-for` can depend on it. A node whose startup config was rejected never becomes healthy. A `healthcheck` set in the topology replaces the default one.\n111: \n112: ### Resources\n113: \n114: The kind reads the official image's own environment variables:\n115: \n116: | Variable | Default | Purpose |\n117: |----------|---------|---------|\n118: | `MEM` | 256 MiB + 8 MiB per data interface and vCPU | VM memory (a QEMU `-m` value, e.g. `1024` or `1G`) |\n119: | `CPUS` | `1` | VM vCPUs |\n120: | `DISK` | `128M` | minimum disk size (the disk only grows) |\n121: | `CHR_INTF_WAIT` | `60` | seconds to wait for the data interfaces containerlab attaches before the VM starts |\n122: | `CHR_BOOT_WAIT` | `300` | seconds to wait for RouterOS to answer, for the startup config import, and for SSH before the node is declared ready |\n123: \n124: ```yaml\n125: r1:\n126:   kind: mikrotik_chr\n127:   image: mikrotik/chr:7.24.5\n128:   env:\n129:     MEM: 1024\n130:     CPUS: 2\n131: ```\n132: \n133: KVM is used when `/dev/kvm` is available. Without it the image's QEMU runs under TCG emulation: the node works, but boots several times slower.\n134: \n135: ## Management connectivity\n136: \n137: Management is transparent: the IPv4 and IPv6 addresses and gateways containerlab gives the node's `eth0` are configured on RouterOS `ether1`, and the container's `eth0` is bridged to the VM's `ether1`. The router is the node's management address: SSH, the REST API, Winbox, SNMP and every other service answer on it, LLDP/MNDP work on the management network, and the address in the topology table is the one in the RouterOS configuration.\n138: \n139: The image ships busybox only (no `tc`), so where vrnetlab's [transparent management](../vrnetlab.md#management-interface) redirects with tc-mirred, this kind uses a Linux bridge. The container itself has no address on the management network; it reaches RouterOS for bootstrap over IPv6 link-local on that bridge.\n140: \n141: The management return path lives in its own routing table, `mgmt`, selected by routing rules for the management addresses, and CHR's `ether1` DHCP client is disabled. A default route in the lab configuration, a PPPoE client's default route or a dual-WAN setup in `main` therefore does not cut SSH or REST access to the node. RouterOS's router advertisements on `ether1` carry a zero router lifetime, so no host on the management network takes the router as its IPv6 default gateway; the container joins the management network only once this is in place. The objects carry the comment `clab-mgmt` and are re-applied at boot when the container's addressing changed.\n142: \n143: /// warning\n144: Do not remove or change the `clab-mgmt` objects or the `mgmt` routing table: management of the node depends on them.\n145: ///\n146: \n147: ## Restarts\n148: \n149: [`containerlab restart`](../../cmd/restart.md) and a `/system reboot` inside RouterOS keep the interface names, MAC addresses, configuration and links: the launcher persists the NIC identity in the container on first boot and does not re-run the bootstrap. A plain `docker restart` keeps the router and its management, but Docker deletes the node's veth links, which stay down until the node is restarted with containerlab or the lab is redeployed.\n150: \n151: ## File mounts\n152: \n153: For each node containerlab creates in its [lab directory](../conf-artifacts.md):\n154: \n155: * `ftpboot/` - mounted to `/ftpboot`, holds `config.auto.rsc`\n156: * `chr-launch.sh` - the launcher, mounted read-only to `/chr-launch.sh` and rewritten on every deploy\n\n(End of file - total 156 lines)\n</content>",

The r2 health wait is 60s — r2 boots without KVM? Under CI, KVM is available on GH runners (ubuntu-24.04 supports KVM? GH-hosted runners do have KVM). r2 boots quicker since r1 waited first? Actually all three boot in parallel. r2 wait 60s might be tight if TCG. But r1 300s. Hmm, r2 has same boot. 60s for r2 could flake on slow runners (TCG fallback). But CI runners have KVM. Existing suites use similar patterns. Not a finding, maybe coverage note.

165: 	return nil
166: }

168: func preStopPrepareVrnetlabQcowAlias(ctx context.Context, d *DefaultNode) {
169: 	aliasName, ok := vrnetlabQcowAliasName(d.Config().Image)
170: 	if !ok {
171: 		log.Debugf(
172: 			"node %q pre-stop vrnetlab qcow alias skipped: unable to infer tag from image %q",
173: 			d.Config().ShortName,
174: 			d.Config().Image,
175: 		)
176: 		return
177: 	}
178: 
179: 	ctx, cancel := context.WithTimeout(ctx, 10*time.Second)
180: 	defer cancel()
181: 
182: 	// Some vrnetlab nodes rename the original versioned qcow image after first boot and fail on
183: 	// subsequent starts when they try to rediscover a versioned qcow filename. If there is exactly
184: 	// one non-overlay qcow file in / and our alias is absent, create a hardlink alias based on the
185: 	// image tag.
186: 	cmd := fmt.Sprintf(
187: 		`alias="/%s"; `+
188: 			`[ -e "$alias" ] && exit 0; `+
189: 			`src=""; `+
190: 			`if [ -f /sros.qcow2 ] && [ "/sros.qcow2" != "$alias" ]; then `+
191: 			`src="/sros.qcow2"; `+
192: 			`else `+
193: 			`set -- /*.qcow2; `+
194: 			`if [ "$1" != "/*.qcow2" ]; then `+
195: 			`for f in "$@"; do `+
196: 			`[ "$f" = "$alias" ] && continue; `+
197: 			`base="${f##*/}"; `+
198: 			`case "$base" in *overlay*.qcow2) continue ;; esac; `+
199: 			`if [ -n "$src" ]; then src=""; break; fi; `+
200: 			`src="$f"; `+
201: 			`done; `+
202: 			`fi; `+
203: 			`fi; `+
204: 			`[ -n "$src" ] || exit 0; `+
205: 			`ln "$src" "$alias"`,
206: 		aliasName,
207: 	)
208: 
209: 	execCmd := clabexec.NewExecCmdFromSlice([]string{"sh", "-lc", cmd})
210: 	res, err := d.RunExec(ctx, execCmd)
211: 	if err != nil {
212: 		log.Warnf(
213: 			"node %q pre-stop vrnetlab qcow alias preparation failed: %v",
214: 			d.Config().ShortName,
215: 			err,
216: 		)
217: 		return
218: 	}
219: 
220: 	if res != nil && res.ReturnCode != 0 {
221: 		log.Warnf(
222: 			"node %q pre-stop vrnetlab qcow alias prep returned code %d (stderr: %s)",
223: 			d.Config().ShortName,
224: 			res.ReturnCode,
225: 			res.Stderr,
226: 		)
227: 	}
228: }
229: 
230: func vrnetlabQcowAliasName(image string) (string, bool) {
231: 	tag, ok := imageTag(image)
232: 	if !ok {
233: 		return "", false
234: 	}
235: 
236: 	return "clab-" + tag + ".qcow2", true
237: }
238: 
239: func imageTag(image string) (string, bool) {
240: 	if at := strings.LastIndex(image, "@"); at != -1 {
241: 		image = image[:at]
242: 	}
243: 
244: 	lastSlash := strings.LastIndex(image, "/")
245: 	lastColon := strings.LastIndex(image, ":")
246: 	if lastColon == -1 || lastColon < lastSlash {
247: 		return "", false
248: 	}
249: 
250: 	tag := image[lastColon+1:]
251: 	if tag == "" {
252: 		return "", false
253: 	}
254: 
255: 	if !imageTagRE.MatchString(tag) {
256: 		return "", false
257: 	}
258: 
259: 	return tag, true
260: }

Reasoning
All consistent. The `PreStop` skip is safe (qcow alias only matters for vrnetlab-built images; here the disk is the image's own file).

Remaining verifications:
1. `core/register.go` diff — verified.
2. Does `docker pull mikrotik/chr:7.24.5` tag exist? Can't verify externally — not a code defect.
3. `docs/manual/kinds/index.md` — added row. mkdocs nav added. Done.
4. Check the `ssh.robot` keyword `Login via SSH with username and password` exists with those args (try_for). Let me check quickly.
5. Check `tests/common.robot` has `Cleanup` keyword (Suite Teardown Run Keyword Cleanup).
6. Check `node_definition.go` HealthCheck field is named `healthcheck` in yaml (yes, line 136).

Also double-check one potentially real correctness item: in `mikrotik_chr.go` Init, `n.Cfg.Entrypoint == ""` check. Is Entrypoint already populated from the image config? In containerlab, `NodeConfig.Entrypoint` comes from topology `entrypoint:` setting; if unset, it's empty, and the runtime uses the image's default ENTRYPOINT. So for this kind, Entrypoint is "" unless user sets it → launcher used. Good.

But wait — is there something in containerlab that copies the image's entrypoint into cfg before Init? Let me check quickly: `core/config.go` or runtime pull → I don't think so. Fine.

7. `rest_add` case pattern `2??\ *` — shell pattern: `2??\ *` matches "2xx <space>...". busybox ash supports `case` with `?` glob. Good.

8. `is_err` checks for `"error"` substring — the RouterOS REST error body contains `"error":...`. A successful response containing a field with "error" in a value (e.g., user config containing the word error)? Unlikely for these calls. Fine.

9. Check `rest` uses wget `--post-data`. busybox wget supports `--post-data`? busybox wget supports `--post-data` in recent builds. Assume tested.

10. One more potential real bug: `rest_raw`'s `resp_complete` loop: `while kill -0 "$_pid" && ! resp_complete && [ $_left -gt 0 ]`. If timeout+5 exceeds, `timeout` kills nc. Fine.

11. `mgmt_fail` exits 0 — after `wait "$QEMU_PID"`. Since trap TERM INT set, ok.

12. One subtle thing: the trap at line 329 `trap 'kill ...; exit 0' TERM INT` — on TERM, exit 0. When the container is stopped (SIGTERM to PID 1 = the launcher), it kills qemu and exits 0. But `wait` inside trap — busybox ash runs trap after current command completes; fine. Note that qemu gets no graceful shutdown, but the CHR disk is overlay anyway.

13. `wait "$QEMU_PID"` at the end — if qemu is SIGKILLed by docker stop after timeout? Default stop timeout 10s → docker sends TERM (trap: kill qemu, wait, exit 0). Fine.

Now let me verify the ssh.robot keyword signature and common.robot Cleanup.
